import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll read the registered guide, create the infographic first, then assess companion diagrams. I’m using the imagegen, sase_repo, sase_memory_read, and mermaid_diagrams skills for this work.


The guide distinguishes working features from those still being built. The infographic will preserve that distinction and focus on six areas: setup, saving threads, notes, privacy, weekly review, and coming features. Both output filenames are available.


The infographic is saved and checked. Two companion figures look useful: capture linking and its fallback, and the planned send flow with re-preview, Undo, and an unknown outcome. The other sections mostly already have a diagram, table, or short list that answers their question clearly.


Both diagrams passed the Mermaid batch check and fit the PDF page above the 75% minimum. I’m checking the rendered images for readability and tracing each path back to the guide before registering the proposal manifest.


The infographic and diagram manifest are registered. Both figures passed visual review, with PDF fit scales of 92.6% and 96.4%. I judged 20 candidates, proposed two, and rejected the rest as duplicates, simple sequences, or information already clear in tables and lists. I’m recording the result for the linker and using sase_final to finalize the two new files.


Created without overwrite:

- [Infographic](sase/repos/research/202611/bob_gmail_everyday_guide/bob_gmail_everyday_guide_infographic.png)
- [Diagram proposal manifest](sase/repos/research/202611/bob_gmail_everyday_guide/bob_gmail_everyday_guide.diagrams.md)

Both are registered. The report is unchanged. Two proposed figures passed Mermaid 12.0.0 rendering, visual review, and PDF sizing checks: **92.6% and 96.4% fit**. The linker decides placement.

The infographic used built-in image generation with [this prompt](/tmp/gmailfig.RD51vs/infographic-prompt.txt).
